notes: Author claims: the opening continuation retracts a previously held belief about H-spaces satisfying strong associativity and commutativity conditions, expressed through equivalence to Ω^i X for arbitrarily large i, and their correspondence with commutative topological groups. It ends by agreeing with the correspondent’s observations on p. 5.

Author questions: the next paragraph asks for an analogue of the tapis de Dold-Puppe for (1/2) simplicial groups, not necessarily commutative, and asks what form it takes. The explicit question phrases are “je suis toujours intrigué par la question suivante” and “et quelle forme prend-il ?”.

Author claims and program: the drawn relation between an ens. 1/2 simplicial and an ∞-groupoïde is called the ultimate “set-theoretic” version of Dold-Puppe. The text proposes deducing the latter by identifying abelian groups in (∞-cat) with chain complexes in (Ab), then asks for the groups of (∞-cat) and begins to say what happens in (1-cat). This page supplies no proof of those identifications.

Mathematical inspection prompts: the possible left prime before Ω, the raised i versus the baseline i, the two 1/2 qualifications, both arrowheads, the overwritten category/groupoid terminology, the singular diagram endings and the omission of ne … autres … que in H were checked against the ink. No formula was repaired from expected mathematical meaning.

Mathematical checking scope: no targeted proof check, re-proof, computation or formal verification was carried out. The diagram and identifications are recorded as author assertions; ∞-cat and the strictness/equivalence conventions are not defined on this page. The checks list is therefore empty, rather than mislabelling visual comparison as proof verification.
The author page number is 3, and the archive foliation is 148. There is no place/date heading or signature on this continuation page.
The source ends with a partial word and a continuation hyphen. The hyphen is suppressed under the prescribed line-end-hyphen convention; no completion from another page has been supplied.

There are no independent margin notes, separate drawings, insertions or general block deletions. The diagram’s right-hand noun contains the one visible overwriting state. Long apparent horizontal strokes attached to g descenders are not recorded as underlines.
The small second point after p. 5. is deliberately left uncertain. The minute irregular fleck between n’y and a is recorded in the review but treated as a copying speck, not textual punctuation.

coverage: The whole image was viewed once for layout, then supplied half a and supplied half b were each viewed once, in that order. Every physical prose line, all mathematical symbols, the diagram, its overwritten word, the continuation ending, both page numbers and the margins were compared against both full witnesses. Nine unresolved places received one tight enlarged crop each; no decided half was re-enlarged and no place was re-cropped. C doubts in grossière, dû and the t/il connector were resolved; the Ω prefix and overwritten word retain localized uncertainty. Agreement between the witnesses was also checked, yielding a residual commutatifs-ending doubt and a possible additional punctuation point. H omits the recoverable correction text and ne, autres, que, changes two diagram singulars to plurals, modernises chaines, and differs in quotation placement and the final partial word. No other independent ink block was found omitted. Archive foliation is only a TeX comment. No OCR, other page, external source, other reader, compilation or delegation was used.
